title: nf-core/metatdenovo pipeline parameters
description: Assembly and annotation of metatranscriptomic data, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns (`sample`, `fastq_1` and `fastq_2`), and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

skip_qc.description: Skip all QC steps except for MultiQC.

trimming_options.title: trimming options

clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 1 (or single-end reads).

clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 2 (paired-end reads only).

three_prime_clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 1 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

three_prime_clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 2 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

save_trimmed.description: Save the trimmed FastQ files in the results directory.
save_trimmed.help_text: By default, trimmed FastQ files will not be saved to the results directory. Specify this flag (or set to true in your config file) to copy these files to the results directory when complete.

trim_nextseq.description: Instructs Trim Galore to apply the --nextseq=X option, to trim based on quality after removing poly-G tails.
trim_nextseq.help_text: This enables the option Cutadapt `--nextseq-trim=3'CUTOFF` option via Trim Galore, which will set a quality cutoff (that is normally given with -q instead), but qualities of G bases are ignored. This trimming is in common for the NextSeq- and NovaSeq-platforms, where basecalls without any signal are called as high-quality G bases.

skip_trimming.help_text: Use this if your input FastQ files have already been trimmed outside of the workflow or if you're very confident that there is no adapter contamination in your data.

trimming_options.description: all the trim option are listed below

sequence_filter.description: Fasta file with sequences to filter away before running assembly etc..
sequence_filter.help_text: Read sequences matching this file will be filtered out from samples with BBDuk before mapping. If no file is specified, BBDuk will not be run.

save_bbduk_fastq.description: Save the resulting fastq files from filtering

save_bbduk_removed_fastq.description: Save the reads that were removed (matched the sequence_filter reference) during BBDuk filtering

digital_normalization_options.title: Digital normalization options
digital_normalization_options.description: Use these option if you need to normalize the reads before the assembly

bbnorm.description: Perform normalization to reduce sequencing depth.
bbnorm.help_text: Normalization is performed following the example in https://jgi.doe.gov/data-and-tools/software-tools/bbtools/bb-tools-user-guide/bbnorm-guide/

bbnorm_target.description: Reduce the number of reads for assembly average coverage of this number.

bbnorm_min.description: Reads with an apparent depth of under nx will be presumed to be errors and discarded

save_bbnorm_fastq.description: Save the resulting fastq files from normalization

assembler.description: Specify the assembler to run. Possible alternatives: megahit, spades.

user_assembly.description: Path to a fasta file with a finished assembly. Assembly will be skipped by the pipeline.

user_assembly_name.description: Name to give to the user-provided assembly.

min_contig_length.description: Filter out contigs shorter than this.

spades_flavor.description: Select which type of assembly you want to make. Default: rna
spades_flavor.help_text: This option allows you to run an assembly for a different scope. For instance, with `--spades_flavor rna` you will get an assembly for prokaryotic metatranscriptomes, `--spades_flavor rnaviral` for viral metatranscriptomes or `--spades_flavor metaviral` for viral metagenomes. The argument to the parameter will be passed as a parameter to Spades; e.g. `--spades_flavor rna` will be passed as `--rna` to Spades.

save_formatspades.description: Save the formatted spades fasta file

megahit_k_min.description: Minimum k-mer size for MEGAHIT, must be odd and <=255.
megahit_k_min.help_text: Coarser (larger) minimum k-mer sizes reduce the memory needed for the earliest, most memory-hungry MEGAHIT iterations, at the cost of sensitivity to low-coverage or short reads. Useful as a last resort when MEGAHIT runs out of memory on very large datasets. Cannot be combined with `--megahit_k_list`. See [Usage: Assembler options](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/usage#assembler-options) and [Coping with large datasets](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/docs/large_datasets) for suggested starting values.

megahit_k_max.description: Maximum k-mer size for MEGAHIT, must be odd and <=255.
megahit_k_max.help_text: Cannot be combined with `--megahit_k_list`. See [Usage: Assembler options](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/usage#assembler-options) and [Coping with large datasets](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/docs/large_datasets) for suggested starting values.

megahit_k_step.description: Increment of k-mer size of each iteration for MEGAHIT, must be even and <=28.
megahit_k_step.help_text: Cannot be combined with `--megahit_k_list`. See [Usage: Assembler options](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/usage#assembler-options) and [Coping with large datasets](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/docs/large_datasets) for suggested starting values.

megahit_k_list.description: Comma-separated list of k-mer sizes for MEGAHIT, all must be odd, in the range 15-255, increment <=28.
megahit_k_list.help_text: Overrides the default automatic k-mer stepping. Cannot be combined with `--megahit_k_min`, `--megahit_k_max` or `--megahit_k_step`. See [Usage: Assembler options](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/usage#assembler-options) and [Coping with large datasets](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/docs/large_datasets) for suggested starting values.

megahit_min_count.description: Minimum multiplicity for filtering k-mers in MEGAHIT.
megahit_min_count.help_text: Raising this prunes low-frequency (often erroneous) k-mers before graph construction, reducing memory use. Usually a safer first lever than raising `--megahit_k_min` on very large datasets. See [Usage: Assembler options](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/usage#assembler-options) and [Coping with large datasets](https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/docs/large_datasets) for suggested starting values.

save_bam.description: Save the bam files from mapping

bbmap_minid.description: Minimum identity needed to assign read to a contig

bbmap_ambiguous.description: How BBMap should handle reads that align equally well to more than one site
bbmap_ambiguous.help_text:
- `best`: use the first best-scoring site (default).
- `random`: pick one top-scoring site at random.
- `toss`: treat the read as unmapped.
- `all`: keep every top-scoring site, i.e. true multi-mapping.

Each of `best`/`random`/`toss` produces at most one alignment per read, which is what the pipeline's counts tables (including the locus-consolidated table, see `--featurecounts_fraction` below) assume when summing counts per ORF/locus. `all` deliberately breaks that assumption and should normally be paired with `--featurecounts_fraction`.

featurecounts_fraction.description: Count multi-mapped reads fractionally in featureCounts instead of at full weight per site
featurecounts_fraction.help_text: Only has an effect on reads with more than one reported alignment, i.e. in practice when `--bbmap_ambiguous all` is used. With the default `false`, a read that maps to N sites contributes a full count to each of the N ORFs it hits; with `true`, it contributes 1/N to each instead, keeping per-sample totals from inflating.

skip_protein_consolidation.description: Skip cross-contig consolidation of ORFs whose proteins cluster together
skip_protein_consolidation.help_text: Cross-contig consolidation clusters the called proteins and sums the per-locus counts of everything that lands in one cluster, producing `summary_tables/<assembly>.protein_consolidate_<identity>.counts.tsv.gz`. Unlike the locus consolidation it builds on, this is not a no-op when only one ORF caller is active: near-identical proteins on different contigs are merged whichever caller found them.

cluster_min_seq_id.description: Minimum sequence identity for two proteins to be considered the same gene
cluster_min_seq_id.help_text: Passed to MMseqs2 as `--min-seq-id`. Rounded to whole percent for the output table name, so 0.99 gives `protein_consolidate_99`. This is less strict than it looks even at 1.0, since coverage is controlled separately by `--cluster_coverage`: calls that are identical where they align but trimmed differently at the ends still cluster. Conversely a splice-aware caller whose exon boundary is off by a few residues in the middle of a gene will fall below 1.0, which is why the default is 0.99 rather than exact identity.

cluster_coverage.description: Minimum fraction of both proteins that must be covered by the alignment
cluster_coverage.help_text: Passed to MMseqs2 as `-c`, with its default bidirectional coverage mode, so the threshold applies to both the longer and the shorter sequence.

orf_caller.description: Comma-separated list of ORF callers to run. Possible alternatives: prodigal, prokka, transdecoder, metaeuk. At least one of this, `--user_orfs`, or `--user_orfs_gff`/`--user_orfs_faa` must be set; any combination may be set together.

user_orfs.description: Path to comma-separated file listing user-provided ORF calls to add alongside (or instead of) `--orf_caller`.
user_orfs.help_text: This has to be a comma-separated file with a header row and three mandatory columns: name, gff, faa. Each row adds one named set of ORF calls to the run, treated exactly like another `--orf_caller` value downstream. `name` cannot collide with an active `--orf_caller` value, `--user_orfs_name`, or with another row's `name`. Use this for more than one user-supplied set; for a single set, `--user_orfs_gff`/`--user_orfs_faa` below is a lighter-weight alternative -- both may be combined.

user_orfs_faa.description: Path to a protein fasta file for a single set of user-provided ORFs. Additive with `--orf_caller` and `--user_orfs`; requires `--user_orfs_gff` too.

user_orfs_gff.description: Path to a gff file for a single set of user-provided ORFs. Additive with `--orf_caller` and `--user_orfs`; requires `--user_orfs_faa` too.

user_orfs_name.description: Name to give the ORFs supplied via `--user_orfs_gff`/`--user_orfs_faa`. Cannot collide with an active `--orf_caller` value, a `--user_orfs` row name, or the pipeline's own reserved names.

prodigal_trainingfile.description: Specify a training file for prodigal. By default prodigal will learn from the input sequences

prokka_batchsize.description: Size of individual files annotated by Prokka in one batch.
prokka_batchsize.help_text: Prokka usually fails on very large input files. This parameter controls the size of smaller batches for which Prokka will be called. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--prokka_batchsize '8.MB'`

metaeuk_db.description: Path to a reference protein database for MetaEuk, either a protein fasta file or a directory containing an mmseqs2-formatted database. Required when `--orf_caller metaeuk` is used.

metaeuk_batchsize.description: Size of individual files annotated by MetaEuk in one batch.
metaeuk_batchsize.help_text: MetaEuk reloads and searches its full reference database on every batch, so very small batches multiply that fixed cost -- unlike Prokka's batching, where each batch is self-contained. This parameter controls the size of the smaller assembly batches MetaEuk is called on, primarily to bound its peak memory use and to limit how much work is lost if a single batch fails. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--metaeuk_batchsize '100.MB'`

transdecoder_batchsize.description: Size of individual files annotated by TransDecoder in one batch.
transdecoder_batchsize.help_text: TransDecoder.Predict self-trains its coding/noncoding model from the longest ORFs in whatever input it's given, with no way to share one model across batches, so very small batches can train on too few candidates -- unlike Prokka's batching, where each batch is fully independent. This parameter controls the size of the smaller assembly batches TransDecoder is called on, primarily to bound peak memory use and to limit how much work is lost if a single batch fails; set it larger than the whole assembly to recover the exact unbatched, single-model behaviour. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--transdecoder_batchsize '100.MB'`

eggnog_dbpath.help_text: This parameter specifies the location of the EGGNOG database or where it will be created using the --create_eggnog_db parameter. The directory must exist.

skip_kofamscan.description: If enabled, skips the run of KofamScan.

kofam_dir.description: Path to a directory with KOfam files. Will be created if it doesn't exist.
kofam_dir.help_text: If a `ko_list` file and/or `profiles` does not exist, they will be downloaded.

kofam_ko_list_url.description: URL to download the KOfam ko_list file from.

kofam_profiles_url.description: URL to download the KOfam HMM profiles archive from.

skip_dbcan.description: If enabled, skips dbCAN CAZyme annotation.

dbcan_dbpath.help_text: The dbCAN CAZyme database will be downloaded to this directory if it doesn't already exist there.

hmmdir.description: Directory with hmm files which will be searched for among ORFs

hmmfiles.description: Comma-separated list of hmm files which will be searched for among ORFs

hmmpattern.description: Specify which pattern hmm files end with

diamond_dbs.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about Diamond database files you want to use for taxonomy assignment.
diamond_dbs.help_text: This has to be a comma-separated file with a header row and four mandatory columns: db, dmnd_path, taxdump_names, taxdump_nodes, plus two optional: ranks and parse_with_taxdump

diamond_top.description: Argument to Diamond's `--top` that controls the percentage of hits to include in the LCA.

skip_eukulele.description: If enabled, skips the run of EUKulele

eukulele_method.description: Specify which method to use for EUKulele. the alternatives are: mets (metatranscriptomics) or  mags (Metagenome Assembled Genomes). default: mets

eukulele_db.help_text: This option allows the user to specify which database to use with EUKulele. Databases that are provided with EUKulele will be downloaded if not already present inside the database directory (see --eukulele_dbpath). Possible alternatives: phylodb, mmetsp, marmmetsp, eukprot. NB: you can't use this option with a custom database as eukulele will not recognize the name and it will start to download phylodb by default. If you want to use a custom database, please skip this option and specify only --eukulele_dbpath.

eukulele_dbpath.help_text: If this parameter is set, EUKulele will look for a database to use in this folder. If --eukulele_db also is set, the specified database will be searched for in this directory and if it is not present it will be downloaded. If a custom database (see EUKulele documentation) should be used, EUKulele will assume that it is present in this folder - N.B. only works with one custom database (if using a custom database, point to a directory that only contains that database).

save_eukulele_alignments.description: Also publish EUKulele's raw Diamond alignment file, on top of the taxonomy estimation and counts.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
